decision: HONEST RE-BASELINE, NO CANDIDATE. (1) The old streaming negative is NOT stale: every recorded text-path number reproduces at tip within its own noise bands (walls 22.25/1.25 -> 22.22-22.30/1.244-1.247; ttft bands identical; render 0.71-0.87ms/frame vs 0.76-0.79; cadence flush-bound 51ms). (2) #2912 moved the tool-call path exactly where the microbench predicts: worker CPU/delta on 150KB-args streams -65% (0.336 -> 0.117ms/delta; acc->tip neutral), 154x on the accumulator's own classes at 10k deltas, 2x wall on unpaced bursts; zero win below the 8KB EAGER_PARSE_LENGTH (TS-parity design — the common small-tool-call regime keeps per-delta reparse, measured harmless at ~10us/delta inside a 0.10ms/delta event pipeline). Settle/finish costs negligible (0.02ms at 150KB). (3) NEW COST CLASS DOCUMENTED (the render path it feeds): the streamed args preview renders live via the pending-tool card's generic raw-JSON panel — O(args) TUI work per 50ms flush (~2.9ms/frame at 150KB, arm-independent, wire-parse-bound) — below the fleet bar (5.7% of the flush budget at an extreme size; the dominant share is frozen-surface wire parsing; no frame drops, no user-visible lag). (4) Residual per-delta cost at tip (~0.10ms/delta = 2% of the r800 pacing budget) is the event pipeline's clone chain, not the accumulator (1.7% of it at 150KB) — no dominant parity-safe cost, no real gap. Lane recommendation: close as a re-baseline record; the tool-call streaming path is healthy at tip behind #2912; the render-path class and the sub-8KB reparse residue are reported for disposition.
